newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps climb - mogas up $4, CFDs up 8 cts.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps climb - mogas up $4, CFDs up 8 cts.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed across the barrel on Monday, bouyed by strong Brent crude futures.
The gains were helped by Asian demand and extended the firmer tone set on Friday.

Brent crude CFDs rose about eight cents a barrel for this week's dates after a jump of 13 cts a barrel last Friday. This week was valued at about 42 cents under June by compared to talk around 63 cents under a week ago.
The following three weeks were 39 cents, 37 cents and 33 cents under respectively.
Gasoline swaps snapped up $4 a tonne, dragged higher by firm Brent futures soaring NYMEX prices which were over a cent a gallon firmer.
Rotterdam barges traded up to $195 for 1-15 May but swaps were heard in the range $194.50 up to $197.25 towards the close. June talked some $3 a tonne lower.

Heavy fuel rose $2 a tonne to talk around $85 for May barges and was helped by renewed demand from Portugal for up to three cargoes of fuel. June was $1 higher but dealers said the thin physical market had dampened trade.
Low sulphur traded at $89 for May.
Gas oil against Brent held at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums were flat after edging higher late last week. May was bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
